newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2924 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday on a technical correction after hitting a two-year high close of 8.2917 on Tuesday, traders said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2919.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2915 and moved up to hit an intraday high of 8.2914 early in trading. It then consolidated below 8.2920 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2926.
Trading was more active than Tuesday with most business done at 8.2922, traders said.
Dealers said a correction was expected after the yuan hit a two-year high close on Tuesday.
One dealer said the yuan continued its upward trend in early trading on Wednesday on pro-yuan sentiment but it faced heavy profit-taking presssure above the 8.2920 level.
"When the yuan stood above the 8.2920 level, more selling was seen to prevent it from rising," he said.
A second dealer said traders were worried about possible falls of the local currency after it hitting two-year highs on three days since the start of last week.
"That pulled back the yuan's momentum for further rises on Wednesday," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2920 level on Thursday.
The yuan closed up slightly at 7.2600 from 7.2830 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0712 from 1.0723 against the Hong Kong dollar.
